sources.authority: Bloomberg News, republished by Bloomberg Law
sources.observedExtract: It reports that, at a company-wide meeting that week, Altman said OpenAI could potentially pace development with several other labs; people familiar with the private details requested anonymity. It says some labs may not agree.
sources.limits: This is attributed reporting of an internal discussion. It does not establish an announced pause, a pact, a timeline, or a product-policy change. The accessible reprint locks the remainder of the article.

sources.claimUse: Attribution and named Anthropic response, if separately stated
sources.observedExtract: Reuters reports Bloomberg said Altman told staff OpenAI was open to slowing development amid safety concerns and might pace development with other labs. Reuters says an Anthropic spokesperson expressed interest in working with the industry on the pace of releasing new tools.
sources.limits: Reuters is relaying the Bloomberg report, rather than documenting an independent eyewitness account of the staff meeting. The Anthropic spokesperson statement is interest, not an agreement or an announced joint action.

sources.observedExtract: Pachocki writes that OpenAI will seek to align, monitor, and build defenses against more powerful systems and will unilaterally withhold further scaling as needed; he says broader interventions will also be needed.
sources.limits: This official post predates the report and does not confirm that Altman made the reported staff-meeting remarks, that OpenAI has slowed development, or that other labs agreed to do so.

sources.observedExtract: Quartz describes the report as based on Bloomberg and says OpenAI declined comment.
